vendor: Pusher Ltd. (a Bird company, formerly MessageBird)
product_family: Real-time developer APIs: Pusher Channels (bi-directional pub/sub messaging) and Pusher Beams (push notifications for iOS and Android). Operated under Bird (formerly MessageBird) since the November 2020 acquisition.

certifications.name: ISO/IEC 27001
certifications.proof_quote: Pusher infrastructure and the products associated are ISO/IEC 27001:2013 certified. Our security program, management system, controls and the implementation of those are audited at least twice per year by an independent and qualified third party, evidenced by the valid ISO27001:2013 certificate.

certifications.name: SOC 2 Type I
certifications.proof_quote: Bird security overview coverage table explicitly shows 'Mobile Push Beams & Channels (Pusher)' does NOT have SOC 2 Type I coverage, unlike most other Bird services (SMS, Conversation Channels, etc.).

certifications.name: SOC 2 Type II
certifications.proof_quote: Bird security overview coverage table explicitly shows 'Mobile Push Beams & Channels (Pusher)' does NOT have SOC 2 Type II coverage.

certifications.name: GDPR (posture)
certifications.proof_quote: MessageBird conducts its business in accordance with all applicable laws and regulations, including General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR). A Data Processing Annex is available on the MessageBird legal pages.

certifications.name: HIPAA
certifications.proof_quote: Pusher does not currently sign Business Associate Agreements with customers. Pusher claims the HIPAA conduit exception: 'Pusher Channels is a mere conduit... it does not store the data field of triggered events.' No BAA is offered and no formal HIPAA certification exists.

certifications.name: PCI DSS
certifications.proof_quote: No public evidence of PCI DSS certification or scoping in any Pusher or Bird security documentation reviewed.

certifications.name: CSA STAR (certification)
certifications.proof_quote: A completed Consensus Assessments Initiative Questionnaire (CAIQ) is available on request as part of the Compliance Assessment package. This is a self-assessment artifact, not a formal CSA STAR Level 1 or Level 2 certification.

certifications.name: ISO/IEC 27017
certifications.proof_quote: No public evidence of ISO 27017 (cloud security controls) certification in any Pusher or Bird security documentation reviewed.

certifications.name: ISO/IEC 27018
certifications.proof_quote: No public evidence of ISO 27018 (PII in public cloud) certification in any Pusher or Bird security documentation reviewed.

certifications.name: ISO/IEC 42001 (AI governance)
certifications.proof_quote: No public evidence of ISO 42001 AI governance certification. Pusher is a transport/messaging layer and does not present AI features.

certifications.name: FedRAMP
certifications.proof_quote: No public evidence of FedRAMP authorization in any Pusher or Bird security documentation reviewed.

privacy.ai_training_note: Bird privacy policy explicitly states: 'No personal data or interactions are used to train or improve LLM service provider models.' Pusher's core transport architecture makes customer-data training a non-issue in practice: data passed through Pusher APIs is ephemeral and not stored, except Cache Channels where values are held in memory only for up to 30 minutes.
privacy.data_region: 9 public global cluster locations (includes US and EU). Dedicated clusters available on request for enterprise customers. Customers should select the appropriate regional cluster to control data routing. Pusher does not track the geographic location of end-client message recipients.

security.name: Encryption in transit
security.value: All data passed through Pusher is encrypted in transit. End-to-end encryption (E2EE) channels are also available, preventing Pusher from reading the content of the data field.

security.name: Encryption at rest
security.value: Data through Pusher APIs is ephemeral and not stored (except Cache Channels: in-memory only, 30-minute max). No explicit at-rest encryption statement because persistent storage is not used for message content.

security.name: Penetration testing
security.value: Penetration test attestation letters available under NDA for enterprise customers. System is audited at least twice per year by an independent third party.

security.name: Vulnerability disclosure / bug bounty
security.value: HackerOne program via https://hackerone.com/messagebird. Researchers eligible for rewards on valid vulnerabilities.

security.name: Monitoring
security.value: Platform monitored 24x7 by automated systems with a dedicated operations team. Status at status.pusher.com.

security.name: Security reviews
security.value: Full security reviews only available to Enterprise plan customers with a security engagement included in their contract. CAIQ (261 questions, 17 domains) available on request for all.

security.name: NDA-gated documentation
security.value: Penetration test attestation letters require a formal NDA. The Compliance Assessment package (Security Overview, ISO 27001 certificate, Statement of Applicability, CAIQ) is available on request.

products.name: Pusher Channels
products.data_scope: Message content in the 'data' field is ephemeral (not stored). With E2EE channels Pusher cannot read content. Metadata (channel names, event names, connection counts) may be retained for billing and diagnostics. Cache Channels store the latest value in memory for up to 30 minutes.
products.notes: ISO 27001 covered. SOC 2 not covered. No BAA for HIPAA; conduit exception applies with E2EE. Enterprise: dedicated clusters and security reviews available.

products.name: Pusher Beams
products.data_scope: Notification payloads and device tokens processed for delivery. Ephemeral by nature. For HIPAA: use opaque identifiers rather than PHI in notification payloads.
products.notes: ISO 27001 covered. SOC 2 not covered. No BAA for HIPAA.

compare.pricing_model: Freemium with usage-based paid tiers (per-connection and per-message volume). Enterprise plans with dedicated clusters and SLAs available.
compare.data_residency: Regional cluster selection (US, EU, APAC, and others). Dedicated cluster available for enterprise. Customers control which cluster their app uses for data routing.

flags: The ISO 27001 certificate is held by Bird/MessageBird (the parent entity), not by Pusher Ltd. independently. Bird's security matrix explicitly lists Pusher products as covered, and Pusher's own security page asserts it, but the actual certificate scope can only be confirmed on request. Enterprise procurement teams should obtain the certificate and Statement of Applicability.

Pusher's security page (pusher.com/security/) still references ISO/IEC 27001:2013, while Bird's current security documentation references ISO/IEC 27001:2022 for its products. Confirm with the vendor which version currently applies to Pusher and whether the upgrade to the 2022 edition covers Pusher products.

Pusher Channels and Beams are the only major Bird services with no SOC 2 coverage (Type I or Type II). Unlike the SMS, CRM, and Email services in the Bird portfolio, Pusher products are explicitly excluded from SOC 2 scope. Enterprise buyers with SOC 2 requirements should note this gap.

No Business Associate Agreement is available: Pusher relies on the HIPAA conduit exception and does not sign BAAs. Covered entities with healthcare data must validate that the conduit exception applies to their specific use case and should not assume Pusher can be a HIPAA-compliant business associate.

MessageBird rebranded as Bird in early 2024, and Pusher's own site and some documentation still reference MessageBird. Legal terms, the privacy policy, and the DPA now sit under bird.com; buyers doing due diligence should treat bird.com/legal as the authoritative source for Pusher legal documents.
